attributes.name: authority_entry
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory"}, {"name": "name", "type": "str"}, {"name": "provider_ref", "type": "str|None"}, {"name": "templates", "type": "tuple"}, {"name": "facts", "type": "dict|None", "required": false, "description": "{attribute of AUTHORITY_FACTS: value or None}; ciamParentAuthority given as the parent CA's name; None: not read (those attributes not owned)"}]
attributes.purpose: Importer builder: a ciamCertAuthority entry (provider ref, published templates and, when given, what the CA's product says of it: AUTHORITY_FACTS type/state/key algorithm/storage/key ref/parent CA/restorable-until of a deleted CA), operator attributes kept

attributes.name: check_issued_certificates
attributes.purpose: Planner check (estate-wide, silent without an inventory): revoked certificate in use = blocker; revoked unused, scheduled, superseded, missing, unconfirmable, untracked per (CA, cared template), inventoried CA without CRL/OCSP = actions; a certificate (not revoked or expired) whose CA or a CA above it isn't active (ciamCaState, via _ca_state_finding) = blocker when ctx.dst relies on it (users_in), else an action owned by its renewal owner, due by the earlier of the CA's ciamCaRestorableUntil and its expiry; an untracked set under such a CA says so too

attributes.name: authority_rows
attributes.purpose: certificate-authorities report rows: config, state (CA type and state; a deleted CA's restorable-until), key (algorithm, storage, key ref), issued by (hierarchy; else the product's parent CA), CA certificates, templates, endpoints, inventory, owner

attributes.name: read_ca
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "ca", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "get", "type": "callable", "required": true}, {"name": "iam", "type": "dict|None", "required": true}, {"name": "by_subject", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "at", "type": "datetime", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (Imported groups, notices) of one Private CA: its entry with AWS's facts (type, state, key algorithm/storage, parent; a DELETED CA's RestorableUntil as ciamCaRestorableUntil) and endpoints, its inventory from the newest audit report, the templates that report shows as its own with who may request.

attributes.name: ca_facts
attributes.purpose: What Google says of a CA (AUTHORITY_FACTS): type, state, key algorithm, storage (Google-managed HSM / Cloud KMS key), key reference, parent (subordinateConfig, else by issuer subject, else the record's CA by issuer CN), and a DELETED CA's expireTime (purge time) as ciamCaRestorableUntil.

attributes.name: authority_chain
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true, "description": "the record snapshot"}, {"name": "authority", "type": "Entry", "required": true, "description": "a ciamCertAuthority entry"}]
attributes.purpose: A certification authority, then the CAs above it as their products name them (ciamParentAuthority), each once (a loop stops at the first CA seen again)
attributes.returns: {"type": "tuple[Entry, ...]", "description": "the CA and its parents, nearest first; a parent the record doesn't hold ends the chain"}

attributes.name: inactive_authority
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true, "description": "the record snapshot"}, {"name": "authority", "type": "Entry | None", "required": true, "description": "a ciamCertAuthority entry, or None"}]
attributes.purpose: The first CA in a CA's chain (itself, then its parents) whose product reports a state other than active (disabled, pending, expired, deleted, failed); CAs reporting no state (AD CS, Vault, EJBCA) are passed over
attributes.returns: {"type": "Entry | None", "description": "the non-active CA, or None (all active or unreported, or no authority)"}

attributes.name: users_in
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true, "description": "the record snapshot"}, {"name": "cert", "type": "Entry", "required": true, "description": "a ciamCertificate entry"}, {"name": "m", "type": "EnvModel", "required": true, "description": "the environment model (a plan's ctx.dst)"}]
attributes.purpose: The entries using a certificate (certificate_users) that environment m relies on: its own or an inherited base's bindings, and shared entries that apply in it (applies_in)
attributes.returns: {"type": "tuple[Entry, ...]", "description": "the users in m, in certificate_users order"}

attributes.description: From deferred note 3249 (issued.py, file 990; decision 3241 D6). The record holds ciamCaState (active|disabled|pending|expired|deleted|failed) and ciamParentAuthority from aws/private-ca and gcp/private-ca, but check_issued_certificates doesn't judge them. Build: an action per record certificate (or untracked active certificate of a cared template) whose CA isn't active (disabled, expired, deleted, failed, pending), owned by the certificate's owner / renewal owner, due by the CA's restorable-until (AWS RestorableUntil; CAS deletion) or the certificate's expiry, whichever is first; a blocker when a target environment relies on it; a deleted/expired CA's CRL stops being published (relate to revocation observation if the record has it). Consider a parent authority that isn't active (an intermediate under a disabled root). Keep silent for CAs no importer reports a state for (AD CS, Vault, EJBCA). Where: opsdir/opsdir/domains/pki/issued.py (+ checks registration). Acceptance: unit tests, showcase change + golden diff reviewed by the master, docs (ops-directory-model / pki docs).
attributes.name: Planner judging of CA state (ciamCaState) for issued certificates

attributes.description: Action/blocker per certificate whose CA (or parent) isn't active; owner, due date; silent without a reported state
attributes.name: CA state judging in check_issued_certificates
